articles.title: Over 3,000 Run in Chennai's Singapenn Marathon to Combat India's Cervical Cancer Crisis
articles.excerpt: India accounts for 25% of all cervical cancer deaths worldwide, organizers say, as the marathon also promoted the national women's safety helpline.
articles.image_caption: Participants in the Singapenn marathon along Chennai Marina Beach on Sunday. More than 3,000 people joined the run to raise awareness about cervical cancer and women safety.
articles.nri_angle: India's cervical cancer burden and the growing health awareness movement in Indian cities matter to diaspora communities invested in public health outcomes back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Flags Ultra-Processed Food Health Risks as ICMR Data Shows Rising NCD Burden
articles.excerpt: A Union Health Minister's statement in Parliament cites ICMR research linking packaged food consumption to diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular disease as India's UPF market crosses $38 billion.
articles.image_caption: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) logo. ICMR data shows rising consumption of ultra-processed foods is contributing to India's growing burden of non-communicable diseases.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated genetic risk for diabetes and cardiovascular disease, making ICMR's findings on ultra-processed food risks directly relevant to diaspora families maintaining dual dietary patterns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 7 Breakfast Foods an AIIMS-Trained Doctor Recommends for Fatty Liver
articles.excerpt: From oats and Greek yogurt to walnuts and green tea, a gastroenterologist trained at AIIMS, Harvard, and Stanford shares practical morning meal choices to support liver health.
articles.image_caption: A spread of liver-friendly breakfast foods including oats, nuts, fruits, and yogurt. Experts recommend these options to reduce fat buildup and support liver health in patients with NAFLD.
articles.nri_angle: Fatty liver disease affects an estimated one in three Indians, making these evidence-based breakfast recommendations particularly relevant for the diaspora community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Chennai Handlooms to Dior Runways: How Madras Checks Conquered Global Fashion
articles.excerpt: The checked cotton fabric born on India's Coromandel coast has travelled through colonial trade, Ivy League wardrobes and high fashion — and is now finding its way home.
articles.image_caption: Handloom Madras check fabric displays the distinctive colourful plaid pattern originating from Chennai. The textile has been adopted by global fashion houses while Indian designers work to revive authentic handloom production.
articles.nri_angle: Madras checks have been a familiar sight in diaspora wardrobes for decades, and their revival connects NRIs to India's textile heritage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rujuta Diwekar's Three Forgotten Summer Coolants That Need No Electricity or AC
articles.excerpt: Celebrity nutritionist recommends vetiver-infused water, mehendi, and buttermilk as traditional Indian solutions to beat the summer heat without modern appliances.
articles.nri_angle: Traditional Indian cooling practices relevant to diaspora families seeking affordable, natural alternatives to stay cool during summer months
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FDA-Cleared AI Tool Detects Hidden Heart Disease From Routine ECGs, Outperforms Cardiologists
articles.excerpt: Pathway Labs' EchoNext model, validated across 500,000 patients and 20 hospitals, identifies six types of structural heart disease from a standard 12-lead ECG — and led to what researchers call the first AI-detected heart transplant case.
articles.nri_angle: AI-powered cardiac screening could expand early heart disease detection in community health settings, including those serving South Asian populations who face elevated cardiovascular risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How Traditional Diets Shape Unique Gut Microbes in India's Tribal Communities
articles.excerpt: A growing body of research shows that India's indigenous populations harbor some of the most diverse gut microbiomes on Earth — and that those microbes disappear rapidly when diets westernize.
articles.nri_angle: Indo-Canadians' gut microbiomes shift dramatically with westernized diets, with IBD rates six times higher than in India — traditional Indian dietary patterns may be protective.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: What To Do With Old Rakhis: Traditional Beliefs and Eco-Friendly Options
articles.excerpt: Hindu tradition advises against throwing rakhis in the trash. Here is when to remove the sacred thread, how to dispose of it respectfully, and sustainable alternatives gaining ground.
articles.image_caption: Rakhis tied during the festival of Raksha Bandhan. Traditional Hindu belief holds that old rakhis should be immersed in water or tied to a sacred tree, never thrown in the garbage.
articles.nri_angle: Guides diaspora families on respectful rakhi disposal methods that can be adapted to any location, keeping the tradition alive abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How Excessive Screen Time Is Fueling India's Lifestyle Disease Crisis
articles.excerpt: Rising screen use across all age groups is contributing to obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular risks in India, where over 54% of adults are already physically inactive.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians abroad face amplified diabetes risk from sedentary tech jobs combined with genetic predisposition to insulin resistance and visceral fat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Marks 12th National Handloom Day With Awards, Exhibition at Rashtrapati Bhavan
articles.excerpt: President Droupadi Murmu presides over celebrations honoring India's handloom weavers as PM Modi renews his 'Vocal for Local' call for the sector that supports 3.5 million livelihoods.
articles.image_caption: A weaver works at a traditional Indian handloom. India celebrated its 12th National Handloom Day with an awards ceremony and exhibition at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
articles.nri_angle: Handloom textiles like Banarasi silks and Kanchipuram sarees remain cultural staples at NRI weddings and festivals, connecting the diaspora to regional heritage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The 'Pink Flags' of Postpartum Psychosis Every Family Should Know
articles.excerpt: As the Lindsay Clancy trial grips the nation, psychiatrists urge families to recognize subtle warning signs before a mental health crisis escalates.
articles.image_caption: A new mother holds her infant in a hospital setting. Experts say the highest-risk window for postpartum psychosis falls in the first weeks after birth, when most mothers have limited medical follow-up.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian-American survivor Kriti Lodha and advocate Aaisha Alvi spotlight the condition and cultural stigma around maternal mental health in diaspora communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Smriti Irani's Viral Motherhood Speech Moves Anand Mahindra to Tears
articles.excerpt: The actress-turned-politician's raw take on raising children — 'You're raising someone to forget you' — struck a universal chord, drawing an emotional response from industrialist Anand Mahindra.
articles.nri_angle: Irani's speech on the tension between holding on and letting go resonates deeply with diaspora mothers navigating cultural expectations of parenting while raising children far from extended family.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How AI Is Pushing India From Reactive to Preventive Healthcare
articles.excerpt: From rural TB screening to AI chatbots bridging the doctor shortage, India is deploying artificial intelligence to overhaul a healthcare system that serves 1.4 billion people.
articles.nri_angle: NRI healthcare professionals and investors are increasingly involved in India's health-tech ecosystem, with many diaspora-led startups building AI diagnostic tools for the Indian market — making this a sector where diaspora expertise directly shapes outcomes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Occupational Pesticide Exposure Linked to 70 Percent Higher Risk of ALS
articles.excerpt: A population-based study found that workers exposed to pesticides faced significantly elevated odds of developing motor neurone disease, with risk climbing alongside duration of exposure.
articles.nri_angle: India is among the world's largest pesticide consumers; agricultural workers in India face high exposure levels, making these findings directly relevant to public health policy on the subcontinent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Antioxidant Could Be Key to Keeping Aging Muscles Strong, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Astaxanthin, found in salmon and shrimp, rejuvenated aged human muscle stem cells in laboratory studies — but with a notable sex difference that could reshape treatment approaches.
articles.nri_angle: Sarcopenia is a growing concern in India's aging population; astaxanthin research has implications for nutritional supplements widely consumed by the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Experimental Drug Force-Feeds Cancer Cells Sugar Until They Self-Destruct
articles.excerpt: A University of Texas team developed a first-in-class molecule that overactivates a key metabolic enzyme, turning tumors' glucose addiction into a fatal weakness.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin researchers are well-represented in U.S. cancer research; advances in metabolic oncology carry implications for cancer treatment globally, including in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Europe's Deadly Heatwave Puts All Italian Cities on Red Alert as Energy Crisis Deepens
articles.excerpt: Italy issues unprecedented top-level heat warning for all 27 major cities as Austria sets temperature records, Hungary shuts down its nuclear plant, and the EU counts over €15 billion in wildfire damage.
articles.nri_angle: Indian travellers and students across Europe face severe heat disruptions, with public transport delays, event cancellations, and health advisories affecting summer travel plans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FDA Approves First mRNA Flu Vaccine From Moderna for Adults Over 50
articles.excerpt: The approval of mFlusiva marks a milestone for mRNA technology beyond COVID-19, giving older Americans a flu shot that was 27% more effective than standard vaccines in clinical trials.
articles.nri_angle: Indian American seniors over 50, a fast-growing demographic, gain a more effective flu vaccine option relevant given elevated cardiovascular risks in South Asian adults.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vanderbilt Team Builds AI Agent to Fast-Track Alzheimer's Treatment Referrals
articles.excerpt: An adaptive AI system aims to close the gap between new disease-modifying drugs and the primary care bottleneck that leaves most eligible patients undiagnosed.
articles.nri_angle: India has 8.8 million people living with dementia, projected to reach 17 million by 2036; AI screening tools could be adapted for Indian clinical settings where specialist shortages are acute.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Erectile Dysfunction Drugs Linked to 85% Higher Risk of Serious Eye Conditions, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A large epidemiological study from UBC confirms what case reports had long suggested: regular use of Viagra, Cialis, and similar drugs significantly raises the risk of three vision-threatening conditions.
articles.image_caption: A new study links PDE5 inhibitor medications to increased risk of serious eye conditions
articles.nri_angle: With millions of PDE5 inhibitor prescriptions written globally, the findings are relevant to health-conscious readers across the diaspora who may use these common medications.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Japan's 'Human Refrigerator' Offers Rapid Cooling as Deadly Heatwaves Intensify
articles.excerpt: A walk-in cooling booth that chills the body in five minutes is already showing up in public spaces and worksites as Japan grapples with record hospitalizations from heat stroke.
articles.nri_angle: India faces similar extreme heat challenges; the innovation could inspire cooling solutions for Indian cities and workplaces grappling with deadly heatwaves.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Largest Genetic Study of Fibromyalgia Confirms It Is a Nervous System Disorder, Not Autoimmune
articles.excerpt: An international team analysed DNA from 2.5 million people, identified 26 risk genes concentrated in the brain and nerves, and found a surprising link to the gene behind Huntington's disease.
articles.nri_angle: The study offers hope to fibromyalgia patients worldwide, including in South Asian communities where chronic pain conditions are often stigmatised or dismissed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bioengineered Chewing Gum Wiped Out 93% of Cancer-Linked HPV in Patient Samples, Penn Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A plant-based gum made from lablab beans eliminated oral HPV and two bacterial species tied to head and neck cancer without harming beneficial microbes, researchers say.
articles.nri_angle: Affordable plant-based cancer prevention tools could benefit Indian diaspora communities where oral cancer rates are among the world's highest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fast Walkers Over 80 Cut Cognitive Decline Risk by Half, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A Neurology study of nearly 4,000 older adults found that 'super movers' maintained sharper minds even when their brains showed similar levels of dementia-related damage.
articles.nri_angle: Walking is the most common form of exercise among older Indian adults, and the study's findings reinforce traditional practices of daily walking that are culturally ingrained across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: D&D Pharmatech's Liver Drug Shows Benefits Before Weight Loss, Lancet Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Zabopegdutide achieved MASH resolution in 62.5% of patients and fibrosis improvement in 50%, with key liver benefits appearing before meaningful weight reduction.
articles.nri_angle: MASH and fatty liver disease disproportionately affect South Asian populations due to higher metabolic risk profiles. New treatments are particularly relevant for the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Rare Eye Condition, but Absolute Risk Remains Very Low
articles.excerpt: Two major studies confirm a small increased risk of sudden vision loss for Ozempic and Wegovy users, while regulators in Canada and Australia update safety labels.
articles.nri_angle: GLP-1 drugs are widely used among the Indian diaspora for diabetes and weight management, making awareness of this emerging safety signal particularly relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chipotle Pulls Jalapeños From Restaurants After 110 Salmonella Cases Linked to Peppers in Minnesota
articles.excerpt: The chain's stock dropped nearly 10% as health officials probe contaminated jalapeños served across multiple Mexican-style restaurant chains.
articles.nri_angle: Chipotle is among the most popular fast-casual chains for Indian Americans; the salmonella scare is a food safety alert for the large NRI population in the US, especially in the Midwest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Landmark Study Links Rare Immune Cell Mutations to Autoimmune Disease, Opening Door to Precision Treatment
articles.excerpt: Researchers at the Wellcome Sanger Institute used ultra-accurate DNA sequencing to discover that somatic mutations in B cells disable immune checkpoints in autoimmune thyroid disease, confirming a theory first proposed in the 1950s.
articles.nri_angle: Thyroid autoimmunity has high prevalence in South Asian populations; the research could eventually replace lifelong immunosuppression with precision treatments targeting root causes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: To Beat Cigarette Addiction, More Health Experts Are Embracing Vapes
articles.excerpt: Growing clinical evidence shows e-cigarettes help smokers quit at higher rates than traditional therapies, forcing a rethink of public health strategy even as youth vaping concerns persist.
articles.nri_angle: India's 2019 blanket ban on e-cigarettes leaves hundreds of millions of smokers without access to a cessation tool now endorsed by multiple Western health bodies, a policy gap felt acutely by diaspora families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
